subject: SLO & sizing follow-up: steady-state vs burst profile for Vendelix
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@vendelix.com>, Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@vendelix.com>

Subject: Post-call: SLO & sizing check (steady vs burst)

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and the numbers you shared — I want to make sure we captured the workload correctly before Marissa and Dev scope a Dedicated recommendation. Please correct anything that looks off.

Top-level SLOs you mentioned:
- 95p latency for first-streamed token: <= 250 ms (interactive support chat)
- Sustained throughput latency target for full-response completion (95p): <= 800 ms for payloads ~300 tokens
- Streaming requirement: chunked token streaming with start-of-stream within 150ms ideally

Workload characterization (as reported on call):
- Average QPS (steady-state business hours): 18 qps
- Average tokens per request: 240 tokens (mean), 420 tokens (95p)
- Average tokens/sec per request (generation speed desired): ~60 tps/user (we interpreted this as the app wanting ~60 tokens/sec consumption per open session)
- Concurrency (midday steady): ~120 concurrent sessions
- Peak burst (marketing campaign window): short spikes up to 520 concurrent sessions for ~6-12 minutes, QPS peaking ~430 qps
- Background batch embedding job: nightly window (02:00–03:00) producing ~6M tokens across the fleet (not latency-sensitive)

Open questions for your team (need answers to size correctly):
1) For the peak marketing bursts, is the 520 concurrent sessions estimate based on sessions or opened websocket connections? Do sessions maintain an open connection during idle think time?
2) During interactive sessions, are you doing single-stream completions per user (one active generation at a time) or multi-turn parallel generations?
3) Can you share a 48-hour token/QPS histogram (per-minute resolution) or the CSV you mentioned on the call? That will let us simulate sustained vs spike heatmaps.

Next steps we propose:
- Elena/Tom: send the CSV snapshot and confirm answers to the three questions above (by EOD Tue 8/17 if possible).
- Marissa: will draft a Dedicated config (baseline + burst policy) and cost delta.
- Dev: run a quick perf alternative for streaming start-time optimizations if we see many short requests.

Attaching the quick worksheet template (vendelix_workload_snapshot.csv) — fill in per-minute QPS/tokens if you can.

Ben

Redwood Inference

Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications below inline:

> - 95p latency for first-streamed token: <= 250 ms (interactive support chat)
This is correct — our ops team will tolerate up to 300ms for first-streamed token during peak but 250ms is preferred.

> - Average QPS (steady-state business hours): 18 qps
That's for the EU support region per cluster. For the US cluster the steady-state is closer to 24 qps.

> - Average tokens per request: 240 tokens (mean), 420 tokens (95p)
Correct. Most conversational turns are short, but we have ~10% of requests that are long (600–1200 tokens) when agents paste conversation history.

Answers to your questions:
1) Sessions: we keep websocket connections open during agent sessions; idle think-time is ~45–90s on average, so an open connection does not imply an active generation. Peak 520 is concurrent open websockets; active generation concurrency is ~380 at peak.
2) Generations: generally single active generation per session, but we have occasional parallel calls when agents trigger background summarization — estimate parallel in 5% of active sessions.
3) Uploading the 48hr per-minute CSV now to the Drive link you provided. Filename: vendelix_48h_20260816-17.csv

Uploading attachment: vendelix_48h_20260816-17.csv

We want Redwood's recommendation to include an autoscaling burst policy and clear fallback behavior (lower-capacity quantized model) if Dedicated is saturated. Also include cost delta for enabling 60-minute burst credit pooling vs on-demand bursts.

Elena

Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: SLO & sizing check (steady vs burst)

Thanks Elena — received the CSV and started a quick pass. Initial observations from the 48h snapshot:
- US cluster steady-state: 22–26 qps, median tokens/request 215, 95p tokens/request 470.
- There are six short spike events (6–14 minutes) hitting 380–470 qps and concurrent open websockets matching the numbers you cited.
- Nightly batch at 02:00 is visible as a 60-minute sustained window of ~1,200 qps but low latency sensitivity.

Preliminary sizing thoughts (very rough):
- Baseline Dedicated pool: target steady throughput to comfortably handle 30 qps with 150 concurrent active generations, using a 1.2x buffer -> baseline GPU fleet to cover steady sustained load.
- Burst policy: allow autoscale to add additional nodes to cover short 10–15 minute spikes up to 500 qps. We'll size burst to be fast-scaling with pre-warmed instances.
- Fallback model: recommend a quantized C model variant for burst degradation paths with a small quality delta and ~40% lower cost.

Dev — can you run two quick sims: one optimized for streaming start-time at 60 tps user speed, and one for completion latency with 400-token typical responses? Aim to provide wall-clock token/sec and expected 95p tail numbers per GPU config.

I'll draft a one-page config and cost delta for Ben to send Elena by tomorrow.

Marissa
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Quick perf sims attached (summary here):
- Streaming-start sim (model A, fp16, optimized kernels):
  * single-GPU median time-to-first-token: 95 ms
  * 95p time-to-first-token: 190 ms
  * throughput: ~1800 tokens/sec per GPU when handling many small parallel streams (good for high concurrency)
- Completion-latency sim (model B, mixed-quant):
  * median end-to-end for 400-token response: 420 ms
  * 95p end-to-end: 760 ms
  * throughput: ~680 tokens/sec per GPU for 400-token workloads

Notes:
- Pre-warmed bursting reduces cold-launch penalty to ~30s for extra nodes. We recommend a pre-warm pool of 1–2 nodes during high-risk campaign windows.
- For the 520 open websocket peak with 380 active gens, the fleet mapped to our baseline + burst models suggests Dedicated baseline sized for steady with ability to add 6 additional GPUs within 45s to meet the peak.

Attaching: proposed_dedicated_config.pdf (contains node counts, autoscale policy, fallback model config).

-Dev
